additional_checks: The historical coding calculation is 36.5 million x USD 30 x 12 = USD 13.14 billion. The original unit error remains explicitly described as USD 13.1 billion versus $131B.

semantic_review: Nine author judgments are translated in sequence, including operating profit versus revaluation, capital circulation, recovery and depreciation, AGI/efficiency, differentiated companies, applications/coding, international competition/China, power/sovereign funding, and technology/operating/investment success.
All four timing paths and revision conditions are retained, including H1 2027-H1 2028, November 2026-Q1 2027, H2 2028-H1 2029, observation in 2027-2029, and the June 30, 2028 non-fulfillment rule.
The four economic-state cells and the four timing paths remain distinct perspectives. They are not summed into probabilities, mapped one-to-one to years, or used to predetermine company winners.

The recovery axis uses the same business, investment cohort and observation period; ongoing net customer collections must cover planned recovery and firm payments without double counting. Legacy cash and financing provide a buffer but do not move an entity into the left-hand column.
Technology slowing does not erase existing capabilities. Secured financing in the lower-right cell can reduce liquidity risk, but operating recovery must catch up before moving left.

Operating profit, investment revaluation, upstream revenue, ultimate customer cash, financing, project payback and group cash remain distinct; revaluation gains/losses are adjusted symmetrically and pretax/after-tax amounts are not mixed.
GPU depreciation is not a second current-period equipment payment or a second full deduction from free cash flow. Economic lives, accounting useful lives and impairment remain distinct.
Technological progress may reduce older assets' earnings, while better utilization may extend revenue-earning lives. Relative resilience is not a guaranteed winner or a buy instruction.

The prior sixth-point translation ambiguity about whose suppliers retain cash has not been reintroduced. New point 9 states that the companies can create benefits for customers and retain cash themselves, at a purchase price that makes sense.
V1.5 remains the version that withdrew the hard coding-market ceiling; the unit error and absence of proof that deduplicated actual revenue exceeds the old calculation remain explicit.
The brief retains every paragraph of the reviewed V1.9.1 opening and evidence body. Only the new core-judgment section, four-cell matrix and its explanatory paragraphs are inserted.

The author's first-person April recollection remains an author statement rather than an independently verified historical fact. Current observed divergence remains distinct from the future baseline forecast.

Final upper-right-cell wording synchronized: lower prices must expand usage and older equipment net cash must cover investment and payments as planned before shifting toward absorption. Positive contribution cash alone is not sufficient.
Final Chinese clarification synchronized in author point 9 and the brief evidence transition: the company being researched must itself retain cash, avoiding the prior supplier-reference ambiguity.
